Plane Error: The party claims to represent the 'people' (WHO) but serves the 'billionaire' (WHO). This is a fundamental inversion of the stated democratic mandate.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
The gap between the 'voice of the people' rhetoric and the reality of billionaire capture creates a downward spiral into systemic extraction.

November 7, 2026

Australia's MAGA, Far Right, Gina Rinehart

ANTHONY KLAN

Billionaire mining tycoon Gina Rinehart is secretly directing One Nation’s party strategy, according to its former national campaign director.

Sean Black has been captured on covert recordings warning Rinehart’s puppets could be given key political or policy roles if the far-right One Nation wins government, The Age reports.

“The conga line of people that go through the party were all connected to Rinehart,” he states.

In further explosive revelations, Black — a formerly jailed rapist who was “sacked” by Pauline Hanson — claims in the tapes he secretly continued working for the party.

Black, with One Nation for eight years, was the party’s campaign manager from 2023 to April this year, when Hanson announced his sacking under mounting media pressure about his criminal history past.

In June, two months later, Hanson publicly defended Black, stating he had “paid his time” behind bars and that she had only sacked him because she had been pressured to.

It was “a decision that I had to make…because people were saying to me, ‘Look, you can’t keep him, I’ve got to sack him’,” Hanson told The Age’s Inside Politics Podcast in June.

In the recordings, Black says Hanson fought against his removal and indicated “she would have me back in a heartbeat once things died down”.

Black says he was only removed from the role because of media pressure, and not because of his criminal past — and that he secretly remained as a key fundraiser.

In the tapes Black said his family firm Front Door Services was helping One Nation’s Victorian branch raise funds for the November 28 state election, in a “consulting” deal where Black could keep a cut of every donation his company raised.

“It was a written contractual agreement…on behalf of the Victorian executive, operating as its own legal entity and my wife. They [Victoria’s One Nation office] were calling me like daily for assistance,” he said.

Hanson did not respond to questions, The Age reports.
